extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper-style dispatch describing Allied landings and associated military, political, and social developments in French North Africa during World War II (Operation Torch).

rubrics_metrics.name: Soldier cultural conduct guidance toward Muslim women
rubrics_metrics.description: Quoted guidance from a booklet issued to American troops: "There is no Arab custom which must be respected more completely than their attitude toward women. ... You must not talk to Moslem women. Never, under no circumstances. The most innocent word addressed to a Moslem woman is considered an insult and is bitterly resented by Moslem men."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surrounding explanation emphasizes seriousness: "The difference between peaceful and friendly relations with the natives on the one hand and serious difficulties on the other may depend on whether or not every single one of us understands and respects the very special outlook the Moslems have toward women." It warns that conduct toward Muslim women "may decide the fate of this campaign." The booklet is said to contain a long list of do's and don'ts and a chapter (Chapter 14) giving this warning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soldier behavior: role as goodwill ambassadors, not conquering heroes
rubrics_metrics.description: Prescriptive guidance in the troops' booklet: Americans must not think of themselves as conquering heroes, but as goodwill ambassadors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes bearing in mind local living conditions and customs, acting to foster friendly relations, and remembering that conduct affects campaign success.

rubrics_metrics.name: War Department communique — operational indicators of successful landings
rubrics_metrics.description: Communique points describing measures/indicators of the operation: "1. Landings by United States forces on North Africa... are proceeding according to plans. 2. Several important airfields have been occupied by the United States Army Air Forces and the Royal Air Force. Ranger units are participating in the operation. 3. The lack of resistance encountered at most of the beaches indicated that the French armed forces in North Africa had no desire to oppose the entry of American troops. 4. The forces that landed during the night and early hours this morning are advancing rapidly, and other landings continue."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These numbered items serve as factual criteria reported by the War Department to assess immediate progress: occupation of airfields, participation of specialized units (Rangers), observed resistance levels, and rate of advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press/communication restriction for correspondents
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported restriction: "The Associated Press and other American correspondents ... were tonight that henceforth they would be forbidden to use Vichy French communications for sending news dispatches."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dispatch notes correspondents were advised they "could remain at" their offices but would not be allowed to transmit via Vichy communications—an operational/ethical constraint affecting reporting channels and information flow.
